<sbproxy-retrieval>
<sbproxy-query>
Which depot handles the aurora shipment, and what access code does that depot use?
</sbproxy-query>
<sbproxy-chunk id="shipping-ledger" score="0.92" format="text">
The aurora shipment is assigned to the Mistral depot; EVIDENCE::shipment-depot=mistral. An unrelated inventory note says that spare canvas covers were counted on Tuesday.
</sbproxy-chunk>
<sbproxy-chunk id="access-register" score="0.88" format="text">
The Mistral depot uses access code cedar-seven; EVIDENCE::mistral-access=cedar-seven. A separate maintenance note records that the south gate was painted last month.
</sbproxy-chunk>
<sbproxy-chunk id="distractor-harbor" score="0.20" format="text">
The invented harbor bulletin discusses blue ropes, empty baskets, paper labels, quiet cranes, and unused tide charts. The bulletin repeats fictional observations about gulls, wooden pallets, and closed kiosks. The bulletin has no operational connection to any shipment assignment.
</sbproxy-chunk>
<sbproxy-chunk id="distractor-orchard" score="0.15" format="text">
The synthetic orchard report lists pear trees, ceramic markers, dry paths, spare ladders, and folded maps. Its second page describes imaginary garden schedules and painted benches. None of these invented notes concerns a logistics facility.
</sbproxy-chunk>
<sbproxy-chunk id="distractor-library" score="0.10" format="text">
The fabricated library memo inventories blank notebooks, brass lamps, quiet reading rooms, and unused catalog cards. It adds several sentences about fictional shelving plans and window repairs. The memo is unrelated background material.
</sbproxy-chunk>
<sbproxy-chunk id="distractor-studio" score="0.05" format="text">
The independently invented studio log mentions clay tiles, cotton ribbons, charcoal sketches, and empty display frames. It repeats harmless details about tables and storage bins. The log provides no answer to the synthetic logistics question.
</sbproxy-chunk>
</sbproxy-retrieval>
